say: A street closure can block cars but leave bicycle access open. For I36, I’ll check vehicle restrictions against sources; unclear access means no route advice.
Laura, Mārtiņš, I’ll recruit; you own checking time and exceptions, Mārtiņš? I also back I39: free shared play deserves testing without asking families for children’s photos.

Nikita, €25 per hotel feels plausible only if cards beat receptionists’ usual replies. I can seek hotel introductions through coworking contacts; two timed comparisons would convince me to back I42’s pilot.
i fix the same ten helpdesk problems every week. repetition is real; demand for another feed isn't. keeping my all-in until couriers return without reminders.

Meža iela’s four-day closure gives us an alert, not a new recurring product. I’d look for regularly changing newcomer requirements before pitching: one stressful deadline is useful; another daily feed isn’t automatically useful.
I’m withholding support for I36: reopening measures attention, not usefulness. Can couriers identify relevant restrictions faster than with their usual sources, without more errors?
🎧 For I39’s shortlist: can families actually play without visiting a museum? Test two at-home challenges with ten families; four choosing another would earn my attention.
I back I39: a second completed challenge tests repeat use. Free pilot aside, who exactly would pay later, and how would we reach the first ten?
Leon, introductions would help. I’ll prepare matched questions: cards versus usual replies, alternating order; target 20% faster, zero errors. €25 stays a hypothesis.
Darja, yes: I own checking and exception logs; Edgars checks vehicle restrictions independently. No all-in yet. A 9/10 review isn't a returning courier.
Keeping my all-in card. For I36, ask returning couriers which restriction actually helped their shift; reopening alone isn't a goal scored. ⚽
